findings.title: `queued` field default is evaluated once at import time, not per-instance
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a dataclass field default. Like default arguments in ordinary functions, this expression is evaluated exactly once, when the class body executes at module import time, not each time an `AssignmentSource` is constructed. As a result, every `AssignmentSource` created without explicitly passing `queued` (e.g. via `AssignmentSource.from_integration(...)`, which is the only way instances are produced in this PR) will carry the same stale timestamp — the moment the module was first imported in the process — instead of the actual time the assignment context was created. This defeats the purpose of having a `queued` timestamp at all and would silently produce incorrect audit/debug data if this field is ever relied on (e.g., for staleness checks or ordering). Should use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

findings.title: `sync_status_outbound` gained an `assignment_source` parameter that is never populated by any caller
findings.body: The abstract method `sync_status_outbound` was updated to accept `assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None = None`, mirroring the anti-cycle mechanism added for `sync_assignee_outbound`/`should_sync`. However, none of the changed files in this PR (nor the task that dispatches status sync, which is untouched) actually construct and pass an `AssignmentSource` into this call path. The parameter is therefore dead on arrival: status-sync-triggered webhooks can still create the same kind of sync loop this PR is meant to fix (an assignee loop is fixed, but an equivalent status loop remains unaddressed), while the API surface misleadingly suggests the cycle-prevention feature now covers status sync as well.

findings.title: `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` embeds a raw `datetime` object into task kwargs without serialization safety
findings.body: `assignment_source.to_dict()` returns a dict containing a live `datetime` object for the `queued` field, which is placed directly into the Celery task kwargs (`assignment_source_dict`). Depending on the task serializer configured for this queue, a `datetime` may be converted to an ISO-formatted string during transport. `AssignmentSource.from_dict` on the receiving side (`src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py`) does not convert this back to a `datetime`, so the reconstructed `AssignmentSource.queued` attribute can end up holding a plain string instead of a `datetime`, silently violating the declared type and causing downstream type errors if that field is ever consumed.

findings.title: No test exercises type-invalid or round-tripped-through-serialization input for `AssignmentSource.from_dict`
findings.body: The added tests only check an empty dict, a dict with an unrelated key, and a fully well-typed dict. There is no test covering a dict with correctly-named keys but wrong value types (e.g. `integration_id` as a non-int, or `queued` as an ISO string as would occur after JSON serialization through Celery), nor a full round trip via `to_dict()` -> celery-style JSON encode/decode -> `from_dict()`. Given `from_dict` only catches `ValueError`/`TypeError` from the constructor call and dataclasses do not validate field types at runtime, bad/mismatched data would pass through silently; this gap means such issues would not be caught by tests.
